transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-03 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Desai (CTO - Argentum Bio), Rafael Gomez (Platform Lead), Nora Hale (Senior ML Eng)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Call focused on scoping a performance POC: identify SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), collect workload samples, define bench harness and timeline. Agreed action items and owners.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros then we'll jump into what success looks like for this POC.
[00:08] Priya Desai: Hi, I'm Priya, CTO at Argentum Bio. We're trying to embed LLM-driven summarization and question-answering into our analyst tooling, and latency's become a blocker for adoption.
[00:16] Rafael Gomez: Rafael here, I run platform. Key for us is predictable tail latency during peak research hours and cost control for batch jobs.
[00:23] Nora Hale: Nora, I own the ML infra and the prompt set — happy to share token distributions.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Hey, Liam from Redwood, I focus on performance and benchmarking. Today we'll propose a TTFT vs TPOT measurement plan and a harness.
[00:35] Maya Ortiz: Our ask is to come out of this with a measurable acceptance criteria set and a plan for a 1-2 week benchmark run.

[00:45] Priya Desai: Quick Q, when you say TTFT, just to confirm you mean time-to-first-token — the latency of getting any model output back for interactive widgets, right?
[00:52] Liam Chen: Exactly. TTFT = first byte/first token latency. TPOT is total per-token processing — basically steady-state tokens per second and cost per token. Some teams use per-token latency or tokens/sec at p95.
[01:04] Rafael Gomez: We have two main traffic classes: interactive analyst queries (median 6 tokens reply, spikes to 120 tokens) and nightly batch scoring of 100k documents. Both matter but different SLOs.
[01:14] Maya Ortiz: Let's capture that: interactive path needs low TTFT p95 and p99; batch path needs sustained TPOT throughput and predictable cost.

[01:25] Nora Hale: For traffic, we can export a 48h sample from production with token histograms and average concurrency. We'll include the top 200 wild-card prompts.
[01:35] Priya Desai: Timeline constraint — clinical review feature launching mid-May. So we need a pilot results by April 15 ideally. Is that feasible?
[01:44] Liam Chen: Feasible if we move quickly. Typical flow: 1) collect traffic sample and acceptance criteria 2) Redwood prepares harness + config 3) dry run 4) full benchmark window. We can aim to complete by April 12 if artifacts are shared this week.
[01:58] Rafael Gomez: Cost sensitivity: if we can achieve p95 TTFT < 250ms for interactive on Dedicated with fallback to Hosted at p99 < 600ms, that's acceptable. For batch, we want TPOT throughput target that achieves a cost per 1k tokens less than our current on-prem $x baseline — we'll share exact numbers.
[02:18] Maya Ortiz: Let's translate those into measurable SLO hypothesis. Proposed hypotheses:
- Interactive TTFT p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms on Dedicated baseline; fallback path p99 < 700ms.
- TPOT batch: sustain 2500 tokens/sec per GPU pod at p95 across 30-minute sustained run; cost per 1M tokens below agreed threshold.
[02:40] Priya Desai: Those sound reasonable but p99 for interactive at 500ms might be optimistic for long responses. We care about first token though — if we get a first token fast, UX is acceptable even if total generation time is longer.
[02:54] Liam Chen: Right, that's why we separate TTFT (first token) from total completion. For the benchmark we'll measure: TTFT p50/p95/p99, per-token throughput (tokens/sec) p50/p95, end-to-end completion times for sampled prompt distribution, and also token cost.
[03:10] Nora Hale: How do you handle KV cache warmup? Our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes for the summarization flow.
[03:15] Liam Chen: We'll run two modes: cold-start (no KV cache) and warmed-run (cache enabled). We'll capture cache hit ratio and show delta in TTFT/TPOT. We'll also vary batch sizes and concurrency to find operating points.
[03:28] Priya Desai: On the Dedicated vs Hosted question — is there an automatic fallback if Dedicated saturates? We need graceful degradation.
[03:34] Maya Ortiz: Yes — Redwood's routing policy can failover to hosted variants with compatible model family. For the POC we'll simulate Dedicated saturation and validate fallback latencies.
[03:44] Rafael Gomez: Ok, important for compliance: we need to see audit logs, SSO integration, and KMS details before any private deployment. Maya can you send the SOC2/ISO checklist?
[03:53] Maya Ortiz: Absolutely — will attach SOC 2 overview and the KMS integration notes.
[03:58] Liam Chen: Back to measurement plan: I propose the following measurement slices: small replies (<32 tokens), medium (32-128), long (>128). We'll drive synthetic and replayed traffic from your 48h sample. For batch we'll do scaling runs at 1x, 2x, 5x observed peak to test headroom.
[04:17] Priya Desai: For sampling, please keep the replay faithful. We use variable-length context (some inputs 8k tokens) — are there memory/seq-len implications?
[04:27] Liam Chen: We'll note sequence-length distribution. For the POC we'll select representative context lengths: short (<=512), medium (512-2048), long (>2048) but if your model uses 8k we'll include a small set to measure tail behavior. Some kernels degrade after 4k, so we need to capture that.
[04:44] Nora Hale: We also want to include the rerank / embedding flows which are high-throughput but small responses; that'll stress TPOT primarily.
[04:52] Maya Ortiz: Good call. We'll include an embedding-only microbenchmark for token-less workload (embedding QPS and latency).
[04:58] Rafael Gomez: What about metrics collection — do you use client-side timestamps or server-side? Replay vs synthetic can skew observed TTFT.
[05:04] Liam Chen: We'll instrument both. Recommended primary metric is server-side ingestion-to-first-byte at the runtime level to avoid network noise; secondary metric is end-to-end measured from a synthetic client in the customer's region to capture real-world e2e latency. We'll provide the harness for both.
[05:20] Priya Desai: For p95 and p99, do you produce confidence intervals or just raw aggregates? We want to be sure a single outlier doesn't sway the p99.
[05:29] Liam Chen: We'll report empirical p95/p99 plus bootstrapped CIs over the run windows and provide raw trace samples for outlier analysis. We'll also flag environmental events (GC, node restarts).
[05:40] Maya Ortiz: On acceptance criteria, should we make a pass/fail matrix? e.g., TTFT p95 under X AND TPOT sustained above Y for Z minutes.
[05:47] Priya Desai: Yes, we need a matrix mapping to business impact. Example: TTFT p95 < 250ms = good; if 250-500ms then acceptable; >500ms fails. For batch TPOT we need at least 70% of expected throughput to be accepted.
[05:59] Rafael Gomez: I want to caveat that our internal baseline numbers might be off in the spreadsheet I shared. Nora will confirm.
[06:06] Nora Hale: I'll export the token histogram and concurrency numbers today. Also I'll add our current cost per million tokens so you can compare.
[06:12] Liam Chen: Great. On the bench harness: we use an open-source load generator plus a recorder that emits CSVs with timestamped events and per-request metadata: prompt id, seq len, TTFT, tokens out, backend node id. We'll share a sample config and a link to the harness repo.
[06:26] Priya Desai: Would you run the bench on our VPC (private) or from Redwood infra for the initial run?
[06:31] Liam Chen: For the first run we usually run on Redwood Dedicated staging infra to iterate quickly. For final validation we can spin up a run inside your VPC (Private) or run through a peered test network so results include network hop. We'll label runs accordingly (staging vs in-region).
[06:45] Maya Ortiz: Let's talk about artifacts to exchange: 1) 48h sample + token histogram (Argentum), 2) acceptance criteria and business thresholds (Argentum), 3) harness configs + scripts (Redwood), 4) SOC2/KMS/security doc (Redwood).
[06:59] Rafael Gomez: On the business thresholds — we'll provide TTFT targets and cost ceilings. Also want to understand how quantization or model variants will affect quality. We need to include basic quality checks in the bench.
[07:09] Liam Chen: We'll include a small eval set (10-50 prompts) to check response quality and automatic similarity scoring against a golden set. If quantized variants deviate beyond threshold we'll mark them as N/A.
[07:20] Priya Desai: What about p99 for TPOT — is that meaningful for batch? I think TPOT p95 is more useful.
[07:27] Liam Chen: Agreed. For batch we'll emphasize p95 tokens/sec over sliding windows (1m, 5m) and 95th percentile of end-to-end throughput. p99 is noisy for sustained batch.
[07:36] Maya Ortiz: Ok, timeline recap: Argentum to share traffic and thresholds by 2027-03-08. Redwood will deliver harness + plan by 2027-03-10. Schedule 2-hour dry run and a 4-hour benchmark window week of March 15. Deliver final report by April 9. Is that acceptable?
[07:50] Priya Desai: That works, assuming action items are met.
[07:53] Rafael Gomez: We'll block time the week of the 15th.
[07:56] Nora Hale: I'll get the exports today and drop them in the shared drive link.
[08:00] Maya Ortiz: I'll send the meeting notes and the SOC2 checklist. Liam will share the harness link.
[08:05] Priya Desai: Quick follow-up on fallback testing — can you simulate multi-region failover? Our users are US + EU, we need to see cross-region route latencies.
[08:14] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll run a multi-region test and capture routing latencies. We'll also validate TTLs and cache invalidation impact.
[08:22] Priya Desai: Any blockers with HIPAA or data sensitivity? Some of our prompts include PHI in examples.
[08:28] Maya Ortiz: We do have a private on-prem option and VPC with KMS — for POC we recommend redacting PHI in sample prompts; if you need real-data runs, we can run in your VPC with our Private deployment and sign a DPA addendum. We'll provide legal contact.
[08:44] Rafael Gomez: Noted. We'll start with redacted data. If that looks good, we may run a small in-VPC check later.
[08:50] Nora Hale: One operational ask — include CPU/GPU utilization and per-pod traces in the report so we can map cost to utilization.
[08:58] Liam Chen: Will do. Our benchmark CSV includes node-level metrics and we can supply Grafana snapshots.
[09:05] Maya Ortiz: Great. Any other questions?
[09:08] Priya Desai: No, thanks — excited to see the harness.
[09:11] Maya Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.
